I’m extremely bullish on AI. I’d use it to eliminate a massive amount of labor if I were building a company today. But there’s a line between automating the work and automating the judgment. Get that wrong and you just make bad decisions faster. Swipe through. I’ll show you exactly where I draw the line. If I were starting over, I would automate aggressively. But I would keep the founder in the loop everywhere taste, positioning, creativity or a consequential decision could change the trajectory of the company. That’s the system I teach in my free AI masterclass. I’ll show you where I’d use AI, where I’d use agents, where I’d keep a human in the loop, and how I’d use the whole thing to go from an idea to a real business without building a 1,300-person company. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

If you're building something new right now, I'd bet your week looks a lot like this. You get home from the job that pays the bills, open the laptop, and do the same thing you did last night, answering the same customer question, fixing the same page, sending the same follow-up to someone who probably won't reply, while everyone online seems to be announcing their big launch. It feels like nothing is happening. I know that feeling. We started Quest making protein bars by hand in a small kitchen. We had no idea if anyone would care. Nobody was clapping. There was no launch moment. There was just the next batch. I wish someone had told me back then that boredom is what progress feels like from the inside. Answer that customer’s question one more time and you learn a little more about what's really bugging people. Fix the landing page again and it gets a little easier to buy from you. If you keep going, one of those reps turns into the thing people pay for. If you stop, you never find out which one it was. It might never get exciting. You just get better at the boring thing, and one day the boring thing starts paying you back. If you want help carrying some of that load, that's what my free masterclass is for. I'll show you how to use AI to take a lot of the repetitive work off your plate, so you have more left for the part only you can do. Thursday, October 8, 1pm Pacific. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to save your spot.

43% of founders said their Shark Tank deal fell apart after filming. Here's how to prep like you're walking into the Tank, so your business holds up when a real investor starts asking questions. I'd argue the process of pitching the Sharks is worth more than the handshake. You get five investors who have sat through years of pitches, all hunting for the weak spot in your business at the same time. You can get grilled by AI Sharks before you pitch anyone, and find the holes in your business while they still cost nothing to fix. PUT YOUR IDEA IN THE TANK [BEGIN PROMPT] You are five Shark Tank investors hearing my pitch. You're investing your own money, so you don't care about my feelings. What I sell: [product] Who buys it: [customer] What it costs me to make or deliver: [cost] What I charge: [price] Sales so far: [number, or "none yet"] What I'm asking for: [amount] for [percent] of my company Each Shark goes after one thing: SHARK 1, THE NUMBERS: Is there real money left in each sale after every cost? SHARK 2, THE CUSTOMER: How will I get customers, what will each one cost me? SHARK 3, THE COPYCAT: What stops a bigger company from copying me in six months? SHARK 4, THE FOUNDER: Why am I the right person to build this? What am I avoiding? SHARK 5, THE DEAL: Is my valuation real or a fantasy? What would you actually offer? One Shark at a time. Ask your hardest question first, then wait for my answer. If my answer is weak, say so and ask again. At the end, each Shark says "I'm in" or "I'm out" and gives the one reason why. Then tell me the 3 things I'd have to fix to get a real yes. [END PROMPT] DON'T LET IT GO EASY ON YOU AI wants you to like it. Ask it if your idea is good and it will often find a way to say yes, you're brilliant. Push back: "You're going easy on me. Do it again like it's your own money and you've lost money on a deal like this before." The Sharks tell you what's broken. In my free masterclass, I'll show you what to do next. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

Quest Nutrition grew 57,000% in three years. I still almost torched the company trusting my gut over a simple test. California was in a brutal drought. Almonds take a lot of water to grow, and they were in almost every bar we made. We saw the problem coming. Where we screwed up was deciding how big to bet on being right. We signed huge contracts to lock in our almond supply before things got worse. The logic made sense: if the drought continued, almonds would get harder to source and more expensive. But we weren’t just betting on the drought. We were betting on exactly how bad it would get, how long it would last, what would happen to prices, and how much inventory we’d need. We ended up walking away from some of those contracts. It cost us A LOT of money. If I were making that call today, I’d make AI pressure-test the bet before I signed anything. Copy this: [BEGIN PROMPT] Here’s what I believe will happen: [trend + evidence] Here’s the move I want to make because of it: [cost, commitment, timeline] Assume I’m directionally right. Now try to break the bet. 1. WHAT AM I MISSING? What assumptions am I treating like facts? 2. HOW DO I STILL LOSE? Show me how I could be right about the trend and wrong about timing, magnitude, price, demand, or execution. 3. WHAT’S THE DOWNSIDE? Give me painful and catastrophic scenarios. Estimate money lost, time to recover, and what else breaks. 4. MAKE THE BET SMALLER. Give me the smallest reversible move that still protects the upside. 5. TELL ME WHEN TO BET MORE OR WALK. Give me measurable signals, thresholds, or dates. No vague feelings. If you can access current data, use it and cite it. Flag anything you can’t verify. Don’t reassure me. Try to break the decision. [END PROMPT] AI won’t make uncertainty disappear. It can force you to see where you’ve confused a good prediction with a good bet. That’s one of the systems I teach in my free AI masterclass, along with the 5-person AI team I’d use to build a business today. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

Agents are becoming insanely powerful. I see way too many founders racing to build them before they’re business is ready. I get it. The promise is incredible. Give AI access to your tools. Give it a goal. Let it research, write, build, execute, and keep working while you go do something else. Eventually, I think that is going to be a massive part of how companies operate. But we test this stuff constantly at Impact Theory, and there is a problem I keep seeing. If you can’t get great work out of AI while you are sitting there directing it, giving it more autonomy does not solve the problem. I would do the opposite. First, learn how to give AI a very specific job. For a solopreneur, I break that work into five roles. The Researcher finds painful problems people are already trying to solve. The Strategist turns one of those problems into the smallest test that can prove whether people actually care. The Copywriter turns that offer into words that make the right person pay attention. The Builder gets a simple version into the world. The Marketer figures out how to get it in front of people and turn attention into customers. Then you stay in the loop. You challenge bad answers. You add context. You make it prove its claims. You tell it when the copy sucks. You run another iteration. You learn what great output looks like. Once you can reliably direct the work, then start asking which pieces should run without you. On Thursday, October 8th, I’m teaching my free AI Masterclass live, where I’ll walk you through exactly how I use this five-part system to go from an idea to something you can actually test in the market. And we’re completely updating the free live-attendee bonus for October 2026 to reflect how fast these tools have changed. If you’re still trying to figure out how to actually use AI to build something instead of just screwing around with it, come to the class. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

I started my first full time job as a copywriter, and for three years I wrote copy that didn't work, over and over, until I learned what did. By the time I left as partner and CMO, I could read a draft and feel where it would fail, because I'd already written that exact failure a thousand times. Now AI writes the first draft for everybody. And the first draft AI hands you is garbage almost every time. Swipe through for the 5-step loop to speed through your 3 years of writing bad copy and get good faster. This works on headlines, social posts, emails, anything you'd normally let AI write. This is one piece of what I teach in my free AI masterclass. I'll show you how to run a 5-person AI team in Claude or ChatGPT, and how to push past the garbage first draft so what it builds for you actually holds up. Thursday, October 8, 1pm Pacific. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

AI is making one type of entrepreneur incredibly powerful. It’s not the best coder. And it’s not the guy with 500 prompts saved in his notes app. Until very recently, there was a hard ceiling on how much one person could actually get done. You could understand your customer, see the product opportunity, know what the offer should be, have strong instincts about marketing, spot the operational bottleneck, and still spend half your life waiting on somebody else. That bottleneck is opening. When we built Quest, we eventually had 1,300 employees. We sold the company for $1 billion, but getting from an idea in somebody’s head to something actually happening in the business required a massive amount of human execution. If I were starting again today, I’d still need specialists. But everyone of them doesn’t need to be human. The generalist with good judgment is the founder with the greatest advantage in 2026. The person who knows enough about product, sales, marketing, operations and strategy to understand what needs to happen next. They don’t need to be the best copywriter in the world, they need to know when the copy is bad. They don’t need to be a world-class market researcher. They need to look at the research and say, “That sounds convincing, but you haven’t shown me any evidence these people are actually spending money to solve this problem.” They don’t need to know how to build every system themselves, they need to know where the business is breaking and what the system has to accomplish. That’s where the money is in AI. The distance between seeing an opportunity and testing it in the real world I can collapse. That’s what I’m teaching in my next free AI Masterclass. I’ll show you the AI team I build myself, what jobs I give each one, where I keep myself in the loop, and how I use the system to go from an idea to something real people will actually pay for. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

If I had $500 and 90 days to build a real business from nothing, this is exactly what I'd do. No team. No funding. No connections. Just AI and the willingness to move before I felt ready. The old playbook is dead. It used to take $50K-$150K and a full year to launch something real. AI deleted that entire model. Swipe through for my exact 90-day sequence, including the prompts I'd use at every stage. Save this. You'll need it. I'm doing a free live masterclass on October 8th where I reveal how to build a 5-member AI team and launch your business in 72 hours with ChatGPT or Claude. No experience required. Comment "AI CLASS" to grab your spot (sign up for the replay even if you can't make it live).

Explain your business idea to ChatGPT and it will almost always tell you it's genius. I built a $1 billion company by finding out fast which of my ideas were bad, here's how I get AI to do it for me in 10 minutes. You type in the idea you've been sitting on for a year, hit enter, and it comes right back: "This is a promising concept with strong market potential! Here are some next steps to consider..." Stanford tested 11 of the biggest AI models this year. They agreed with the person asking about 49% more often than a human would. Think about if your AI were a person on your payroll. You'd have hired someone whose whole job is to nod. They never argue, they never ask for proof, and they never once tell you the thing you'd give anything to hear six months before it's too late. A bad employee at least makes mistakes you can see. This one makes your mistakes feel like good ideas. And you're paying them $20 a month! We had our own version of this at Quest. We kept launching fruit flavors. Most of them failed. Then someone in our finance department pointed out something that had been in our sales numbers the whole time. Every one of our best sellers had chocolate in it. We doubled down on chocolate. STEP 1: MAKE IT ASSUME YOU FAILED Paste in your idea, who it's for, and what you'd charge. Then put this line at the top: "Before you answer, assume this idea is dead a year from now. Tell me the most likely reason it died, and argue it like you'd bet your own money on it." STEP 2: GIVE IT YOUR REAL NUMBERS Paste in whatever you actually have. Then ask: "Look only at this data. What pattern am I ignoring, and what would you stop doing tomorrow if this were your money?" STEP 3: PUSH BACK ONCE Whatever reason it gives you, ask: "What would have to be true for that to be wrong?" That answer is your first test. What you do next is what I'm teaching in my free masterclass on Thursday, October 8, at 1pm Pacific. I'll walk you through the five AI roles I'd use to go from a tested idea to a real business. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

AI has made it insanely easy to build the wrong thing faster. If I were starting from zero today, I would not ask AI for business ideas. I’d use it to prove there’s a problem worth solving before I built a damn thing. Swipe for the 4-step order I’d use. This is the system I’m teaching live on Thursday, October 8th at 1 PM Pacific. I’m going to walk through the exact sequence I use, the prompts at each stage, how I move an idea through the different AI roles, and what I’m looking for before I let it move to the next step. If you want to see how I actually use AI to go from “I have an idea” to “I have evidence this could be a profitable business,” come to the masterclass. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up for free.

Before McDonald's lets you open a restaurant, you pay a $45,000 franchise fee. That buys you the right to run a business someone already proved works. Here's how to get that for your own idea, for $20. Before a new owner signs, McDonald's shows them a number. The average U.S. restaurant open at least a year did about $4 million in sales in 2024. Let’s say you're opening a restaurant around a recipe that only you and your mom have tasted. You sign the lease, you buy the fryers, you pay a guy to paint the sign, and then you stand behind the counter on opening day waiting to find out if anyone is actually hungry for what you cook. A smart chef does it backwards. She makes a small batch, hands it out on the corner, and watches faces. If people come back for a second one and ask where they can buy it, she has her proof. The only thing you pay for is a $20 Claude or ChatGPT subscription. STEP 1: FIND THE HUNGER Paste this in: "I want to sell [your idea] to [your customer]. Find the 5 complaints they bring up most on Reddit, Amazon reviews, and forums. Quote real posts. Rank them by how angry people sound and whether anyone says they'd pay to fix it." STEP 2: WRITE THE MENU "Turn this complaint into a one-line offer with a price. Give me 5 versions. Tell me which one a stranger would understand in 5 seconds, and why." STEP 3: HAND OUT THE SAMPLE Ask the same chat for the words, then put them in a free Google Form with a spot for an email. "Write a one-page sign-up form for this offer: [offer]. A headline, three lines on what they get, and a button that says exactly what happens next." STEP 4: COUNT THE LINE "I'm posting this to [where] and I have [audience size]. What number of signups in 7 days means this is real, and what number means I should walk away?" STEP 5: ASK FOR MONEY "Write a short email to the [number] people who signed up for [offer]. Offer them first access at [price]. No hype. Make it easy to say yes or no." Then count who pays. In my free AI masterclass, I'll walk you through the full way I validate an idea fast. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

I can give two people the exact same AI and the exact same task, and one will get something worth betting a company on while the other gets trash. Person one types: “I'm building a protein bar company. Give me a strategy to grow it.” AI comes back with the usual stuff. Build a social presence. Work with fitness influencers. Get into retail. Create a subscription. Run paid ads. That sounds reasonable enough that somebody who doesn't deeply understand the business might start spending money on it. Now give the exact same AI the exact same task, but first tell it what I knew when we were building Quest Nutrition. Who we were trying to reach. What they desperately wanted. What they were already buying. Why they would pick our bar instead of the one sitting six inches away. When manufacturers told us we couldn't make the bar we wanted without high fructose corn syrup, we knew enough about the product and the customer to ignore them, build our own machines, and keep going. That’s why Quest eventually sold for a billion dollars. That little bit of context changes the conversation. Now AI isn't inventing a business for you and then giving advice to the business it invented. It's reasoning about yours. If you leave holes in the context, AI has to fill them. And it will fill them with the most average answer based on companies that look vaguely like yours. Nicely polished trash. Once everybody has access to the same insanely powerful models, the advantage moves back to the person using them. In my free AI Masterclass, I'm going to show you the larger system I use to turn AI into an actual business tool, including how to validate what is worth building, pressure-test your decisions, and build an AI team that can handle research, content and outreach. Comment LIVE CLASS and I'll send you the link to sign up.

STEP 1: MAKE IT ASSUME YOU FAILED

Paste in your idea, who it's for, and what you'd charge. Then put this line at the top:

"Before you answer, assume this idea is dead a year from now. Tell me the most likely reason it died, and argue it like you'd bet your own money on it."

STEP 2: GIVE IT YOUR REAL NUMBERS

Paste in whatever you actually have. Then ask:

"Look only at this data. What pattern am I ignoring, and what would you stop doing tomorrow if this were your money?"

STEP 3: PUSH BACK ONCE

Whatever reason it gives you, ask: "What would have to be true for that to be wrong?"

That answer is your first test.

AI comes back with the usual stuff.

Build a social presence.

That sounds reasonable enough that somebody who doesn't deeply understand the business might start spending money on it.

Now give the exact same AI the exact same task, but first tell it what I knew when we were building Quest Nutrition.

Who we were trying to reach. What they desperately wanted. What they were already buying. Why they would pick our bar instead of the one sitting six inches away.

When manufacturers told us we couldn't make the bar we wanted without high fructose corn syrup, we knew enough about the product and the customer to ignore them, build our own machines, and keep going. That’s why Quest eventually sold for a billion dollars.

That little bit of context changes the conversation.

Now AI isn't inventing a business for you and then giving advice to the business it invented.

It's reasoning about yours.

If you leave holes in the context, AI has to fill them. And it will fill them with the most average answer based on companies that look vaguely like yours. Nicely polished trash.
